## Original idea
{
  "title": "Layout-Structured Multi-Hop Evidence Chains for Complex Document Reasoning",
  "project_name": "layout_hop_evidence_chain",
  "source": "web_research",
  "core_problem": "Complex document questions require synthesizing evidence from multiple layout regions within a single page — reading a value from a table, referencing the adjacent caption, then cross-checking with an embedded chart — but no existing method trains a generative VLM to produce explicit multi-hop traversal traces across Table, Figure, Caption, and TextBlock nodes while preserving typed spatial relationships between semantic layout elements. Models either flatten the document into a token sequence (losing inter-region structure) or navigate page-by-page (missing within-page region-to-region links), or use implicit graph propagation with no supervisable chain-of-thought.

The empirical gap is well-established for WITHIN-PAGE multi-hop layout reasoning: WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) demonstrates that within-page multi-hop table-and-chart reasoning is severely challenging for current models — in the oracle/direct-context setting (table and chart provided directly), proprietary models achieve ~70% (GPT-4o: 71.42%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 70.82%, Gemini-2.0-Pro: 69.53%) while open-source VLMs score only 14–27% (InternVL2.5-78B: 27.37%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 23.17%, Llama-3.2-11B: 14.08%); in the Wikidoc/retrieval setting, GPT-4o is the only model exceeding 50% (55.24%). Notably, the oracle-setting open-source performance (23–27%) is near-random for a 4-choice MCQ (25% baseline) and barely scales from 1B to 78B parameters — indicating a fundamental cross-modal synthesis limitation rather than purely a layout traversal gap. This large open-source gap in the oracle setting directly quantifies the within-region synthesis difficulty that LHEC targets, while the scale-invariance pattern motivates making the InfographicVQA hard subset the primary contribution claim. InfographicVQA's hard multi-hop layout questions (requiring ≥2 layout-region hops across charts, tables, captions, and text blocks in a single infographic) represent the primary per-page evaluation front where base VLMs that treat pages as flat images fail to exploit spatial relationships.

Two prior works come closest. PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) already builds typed Logical Relation graphs (parent-child hierarchical) and Spatial Relation graphs (8-directional: top/bottom/left/right and four diagonals) over document nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — graph construction over these node types is therefore not novel. But PDF-VQA's LoSpa model is fully extractive (predicts an element index via GCN, then retrieves OCR text from that region), produces no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought, and is evaluated only on the proprietary PDF-VQA PubMed dataset. MGA-VQA (arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025) builds a spatial graph from OCR-detected text bounding boxes with untyped proximity/similarity edges and propagates through a 3-layer implicit GCN; its text-box nodes miss figure and chart regions entirely, its edges carry no semantic type labels, and all outputs are extractive spans with no traversal chain-of-thought.

The structured gap is: no method trains a generative VLM to verbalize step-by-step multi-hop traversal across typed layout-region nodes within a page — the exact capability required to answer questions that chain a table value through an Adjacent edge to its Caption and then through a Caption-of edge into a referenced Figure.",
  "opportunity": "InfographicVQA (WACV 2022, leaderboard active) is the **primary** evaluation target and the primary contribution claim: it is genuinely per-page and layout-intensive, requiring joint reasoning over charts, tables, maps, and text blocks within single infographic images. The current SOTA is 88.4% ANLS achieved by Small Drafts, Big Verdict (arXiv:2510.20812, Oct 2025), a training-free speculative decoding ensemble that combines five small draft VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, MiMo-VL-7B-RL, InternVL3-8B, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, Ovis2.5-9B) with GPT-4o as the verdict model — this result requires proprietary inference at test time and a multi-model ensemble. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B as the verdict model instead of GPT-4o, the method achieves 86.7%. The best open-source single-model zero-shot result is Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct at 84.2% ANLS (as reported in the SV paper). No method exceeds 90% (human performance is ~98%), confirming this benchmark is not at ceiling. LHEC targets a complementary and different efficiency point in the design space: a single trained open-source 8B model with intrinsic multi-hop layout reasoning capability, requiring no ensemble and no proprietary model at inference time.

The actual fine-tuning backbone is Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, whose InfoVQA baseline must be established via zero-shot evaluation on Day 1 of the project (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct score is unconfirmed in any public source as of May 2026 — likely in the 80–84 range based on scaling trends from Qwen2.5-VL-7B). Regardless of the overall ANLS level, hard multi-hop layout questions — those requiring the model to traverse ≥2 typed layout regions to compose the answer, identified via InfographicVQA's evidence-source category annotations — are the defensible hard subset where LHEC's explicit traversal training targets a meaningful gap over the base model. The Day 0 hard-subset audit (described in the approach) will determine whether the hard subset count supports statistical significance (≥200) or preliminary (100–200) framing.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) is an **exploratory secondary** evaluation target: it benchmarks multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia. In the oracle/direct-context setting (table and chart provided directly), proprietary models achieve ~70% (GPT-4o: 71.42%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 70.82%, Gemini-2.0-Pro: 69.53%), while open-source VLMs score only 14–27% even with direct evidence access (InternVL2.5-78B: 27.37%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 23.17%). Critically, this oracle-setting open-source performance is near-random for a 4-choice MCQ (25% random baseline) and barely scales from 1B to 78B parameters — indicating that the failure reflects a fundamental cross-modal table+chart synthesis limitation rather than a layout traversal gap that typed graph training alone can bridge. LHEC evaluates WikiMixQA exclusively in the oracle setting; at evaluation, LHEC (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct fine-tuned) receives the HTML table and chart image as direct multimodal inputs without DocLayout-YOLO preprocessing — the trained cross-modal traversal reasoning is applied directly to these two provided modalities. The Wikidoc/retrieval setting is excluded because LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address evidence spread across multiple rendered pages (Wikipedia articles average 24.18 rendered pages). The Day 1 zero-shot Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline on WikiMixQA oracle will establish whether traversal fine-tuning yields non-trivial gains (>5%). If gains are ≤5% over the Day 1 baseline, the WikiMixQA result is reported as a documented negative — establishing the limits of layout traversal training for cross-modal table+chart synthesis — and the contribution is framed entirely through the InfographicVQA hard multi-hop subset. This contingency plan is the expected primary contribution scenario given the near-random, scale-invariant failure pattern.

DocHop-QA (arXiv:2508.15851, NeurIPS 2025 track) is explicitly a cross-DOCUMENT benchmark (its own paper reports multi-document reasoning dominates overall). LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address cross-document failure modes. DocHop-QA is therefore used ONLY as a supplementary training corpus after a Day 1 audit: instances where all BBox-annotated evidence regions fall within a single page are extracted and used for within-page traversal chain synthesis; the cross-document majority of the 11,379 instances is excluded. If the within-page audit yields fewer than 500 usable instances, DocHop-QA is dropped from training entirely and the claim of using it is removed.

BRIDGE (March 2026, arXiv:2603.07931) provides grounded multi-hop evidence annotations for long scientific documents and confirms no proposed method resolves the within-page cross-region gap it diagnoses; it is a strong secondary evaluation target for the AAAI 2027 extended version. The combination of DocLayout-YOLO layout detection (with GT annotation fallback for infographics, detailed in approach) + rule-based typed graph + generative VLM fine-tuned on explicit verbalized traversal chains is architecturally distinct from PDF-VQA (extractive element-index model), MGA-VQA (implicit GCN on OCR boxes), LayoutLLM/DocLayLLM (text layout embeddings with coordinate-anchored CoT steps, no spatial graph), and Small Drafts, Big Verdict (inference-time ensemble requiring GPT-4o), buildable entirely from open components, and executable within 15 days targeting EMNLP 2026 ARR (May 25, 2026).",
  "landscape": "Multi-page document VQA methods include GRAM (learnable document tokens), Hi-VT5 (hierarchical page summaries), Doc-V* (April 2026, arXiv:2604.13731, coarse-to-fine agentic page navigation), AVIR (Jan 2026, adaptive visual retrieval for SlideVQA). Within-page multi-hop reasoning: ARGUS (CVPR 2025) grounds single visual elements with bounding boxes in CoT chains; GCoT (March 2025) generates coordinate-grounded reasoning steps; MAGIC-VQA (ACL 2025 Findings) uses commonsense knowledge graphs for inference.

LayoutLLM (arXiv:2404.05225, CVPR 2024) introduces LayoutCoT, a three-step layout chain-of-thought module (Question Analysis → Relevant Area Concentration → Answer Formation) that generates text reasoning steps augmented with bounding-box coordinate anchors over document layout text, achieving +3.45% on DocVQA zero-shot (74.27% ANLS). LayoutLLM uses a LayoutLMv3-based document encoder with 2D positional text embeddings — there is no spatial graph, no typed inter-region edges, and no visual region detector; the 'Relevant Area Concentration' step outputs the union bounding box of relevant text spans rather than traversing detected layout regions. LayoutCoT does not evaluate on InfographicVQA or WikiMixQA. LHEC extends this direction on three axes: (a) LHEC uses DocLayout-YOLO to ground reasoning in visually detected spatial regions (Table, Figure, Caption, TextBlock) rather than text layout embeddings; (b) LHEC assigns typed spatial edges between detected nodes (Caption-of, Adjacent, Up/Down/Left/Right) enabling graph-structured multi-hop traversal across heterogeneous region types including figure and chart nodes invisible to text-only encoders; (c) LHEC trains on explicit node-ID traversal traces (Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]) that are directly supervisable as structured chain-of-thought, rather than question-type reasoning steps. DocLayLLM (arXiv:2408.15045, CVPR 2025), a follow-on from the same lineage, integrates visual patches (196 tokens), 2D positional tokens, and text into an LLM backbone via lightweight projectors with CoT Pre-training on layout-type, table-structure, and geometry tasks plus CoT Annealing; it achieves 76.59% on InfographicVQA ANLS. DocLayLLM similarly uses no spatial graph and no typed inter-region edges — its table-structure CoT operates within detected table boundaries, not across heterogeneous layout region types.

PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) is an important predecessor that must be cited and differentiated from. It builds both a typed Logical Relation graph (LR graph: binary parent-child hierarchical edges) and a typed Spatial Relation graph (SR graph: 8-directional edges — top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) over document element nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — the same node types LHEC uses. Its LoSpa model propagates via GCN to predict the index of the document element containing the answer (fully extractive: answer is OCR text retrieved from that region). PDF-VQA is evaluated only on its own proprietary PubMed Central dataset and contains no verbalized chain-of-thought. LHEC's novel contribution relative to PDF-VQA is the training of a generative VLM to verbalize traversal traces step-by-step ('Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]') as a directly supervisable chain-of-thought.

MGA-VQA (Nov 2025, arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025 track) is the second closest prior work and the most important direct comparison target: it uses OCR-detected text boxes as nodes (no figure/chart nodes), untyped proximity and semantic-similarity edges with scalar weights, a 3-layer GCN for implicit propagation, and extractive span outputs; it evaluates on FUNSD, CORD, SROIE, DocVQA, STE-VQA, RICO — DocVQA is included but all outputs are extractive spans from OCR boxes; no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought is produced and figure/chart regions are invisible to the model. LHEC differentiates on four axes: semantic layout region nodes, typed edges, verbalized traversal traces, and generative output. Public code at github.com/ahmad-shirazi/MGAVQA enables direct comparison.

GraphDoc (ICLR 2025) annotates spatial and logical relations (Up/Down/Left/Right, Parent/Child/Sequence) between document nodes, providing the taxonomy directly used in LHEC's rule-based edge assignment.

Small Drafts, Big Verdict (arXiv:2510.20812, Oct 2025) achieves the current InfographicVQA SOTA of 88.4% ANLS using a training-free speculative decoding ensemble: a pool of 5 small VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, MiMo-VL-7B-RL, InternVL3-8B, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, Ovis2.5-9B) generates diverse reasoning paths; a consensus mechanism selects 3 draft experts whose high-agreement paths are forwarded; GPT-4o synthesizes these paths as the verdict model. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B as verdict, the method achieves 86.7% ANLS. Individual baselines from the paper: Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct zero-shot = 84.2% ANLS; GPT-4o zero-shot = 76.5% ANLS. The method is training-free but requires proprietary inference (GPT-4o) and a multi-model ensemble at test time. LHEC is architecturally complementary: direct training of a single open-source 8B model to internalize multi-hop layout traversal, requiring no ensemble and no proprietary model at inference time.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) benchmarks multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia (1,000 MCQs from 526 articles): in the oracle/direct-context setting, proprietary models achieve ~70% (GPT-4o: 71.42%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 70.82%, Gemini-2.0-Pro: 69.53%) while open-source VLMs score only 14–27% even with evidence provided directly (InternVL2.5-78B: 27.37%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 23.17%); in the Wikidoc/retrieval setting, GPT-4o scores 55.24% and is the only model exceeding 50%. The oracle-setting open-source failure is near-random (25% random baseline for 4-choice MCQ) and scale-invariant from 1B to 78B parameters — indicating a fundamental cross-modal table+chart synthesis limitation. Evidence pairs are drawn from the same Wikipedia article but may span different rendered pages (articles average 24.18 rendered pages). LHEC evaluates WikiMixQA exclusively in the oracle setting as an exploratory secondary target; at evaluation, LHEC receives the HTML table and chart image as direct multimodal inputs without DocLayout-YOLO preprocessing, applying trained cross-modal traversal reasoning directly to these provided modalities.

HopChain (March 2026, arXiv:2603.17024) synthesizes multi-hop vision-language reasoning data for RLVR training via category identification, instance segmentation, multi-hop query generation, and verifiable numeric answers — it is a counting-task synthesis framework, NOT a document layout traversal chain method, and is not used in LHEC's synthesis pipeline. LHEC's traversal chain synthesis is a custom pipeline described separately.

DocHop-QA (Aug 2025, arXiv:2508.15851, NeurIPS 2025 track) is a cross-DOCUMENT benchmark where multi-document reasoning dominates; it is NOT suitable as a primary LHEC evaluation target since LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address cross-document reasoning. DocHop-QA's BBox-annotated evidence regions are useful as a supplementary within-page training source after auditing for single-page-evidence instances only.

Benchmark papers BRIDGE (March 2026) and DocHop-QA (Aug 2025) diagnose the multi-hop gap without proposing methods. InfographicVQA (WACV 2022): current SOTA 88.4% ANLS (Small Drafts, Big Verdict with GPT-4o verdict, training-free ensemble); best open-source single-model zero-shot 84.2% (Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct); no method exceeds 90% (human ~98%); Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct zero-shot baseline to be established on Day 1; the hard multi-hop layout question subset (questions requiring ≥2 evidence source types per InfographicVQA annotations, Day 0 audit) is the primary evaluation target and primary contribution claim where LHEC is expected to show improvement.",
  "approach": "We propose LHEC (Layout-Structured Hop Evidence Chains): given a document page, DocLayout-YOLO detects all layout regions (TextBlock, Table, Figure, Caption), and rule-based heuristics assign typed spatial and semantic edges to build a per-page evidence graph — no separate relation head training is required, eliminating a 2-4 day training dependency. Specifically: (1) Caption-of edge: from a Caption node to the nearest Table or Figure within 150px vertical distance; (2) Adjacent edge: between any two regions sharing a column or row boundary within 50px; (3) Up/Down/Left/Right edges: from center-point geometry following GraphDoc taxonomy (nearest neighbor in each axis direction). This rule-based assignment is deterministic, requires no annotated training data, and completes in minutes on CPU alongside DocLayout-YOLO inference. A trained relation head replacing these heuristics is a natural extension presented as future work (AAAI 2027 version).

A Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct backbone fine-tuned with QLoRA is trained to produce structured multi-hop reasoning traces that explicitly traverse this graph — citing region node IDs and edge types at each hop (e.g., 'Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]') — before producing the final answer.

**Day 0 prerequisite — DocLayout-YOLO infographic validation:** DocLayout-YOLO was trained exclusively on formal structured documents (academic, financial, legal, and textbook categories from D4LA, DocLayNet, and DocStructBench) and has no training signal for infographic-style documents. Before committing to the synthesis pipeline, we run DocLayout-YOLO on 100 InfographicVQA training images and compute Table/Figure/Caption/TextBlock region recall against the gold evidence bounding box annotations provided in the InfographicVQA training set. If recall ≥60%, we proceed with YOLO-detected regions as graph nodes for all InfographicVQA training data. If recall <60% (the expected outcome given the training domain mismatch), we substitute InfographicVQA's own annotated bounding boxes as graph nodes for the InfographicVQA training portion, reserving YOLO detection for PMC-OA where no ground-truth annotations exist. For evaluation at test time (where GT annotations are not publicly available), we use DocLayout-YOLO in all conditions and report its validation-split recall as a confound in the paper.

**Day 0 prerequisite — InfographicVQA hard multi-hop subset audit:** InfographicVQA annotates each question with evidence source type(s) — Text, Figure, Table/List, Map, Visual/Layout — with multiple types permitted per question. We run the released annotation files to identify test-set questions annotated with ≥2 distinct evidence source types; this constitutes the hard multi-hop subset. Framing gates: ≥200 test questions = statistical significance claim; 100–200 = preliminary targeted evaluation; <100 = drop hard-subset framing entirely and frame contribution through WikiMixQA oracle-setting gains. Based on InfographicVQA's design intent (3,288 test questions across 579 complex infographic images requiring multimodal layout reasoning), we estimate ≥500 qualifying questions (>15% of test set), but the exact count is established before finalizing any contribution claims.

Training data synthesis (custom pipeline — not HopChain, which is a numeric counting RLVR framework unrelated to document layout traversal): (1) Run DocLayout-YOLO over PMC-OA scientific page subset and, if Day 0 recall ≥60%, over InfographicVQA training images; otherwise use InfographicVQA's own annotated bounding boxes as graph nodes for InfographicVQA training data. (2) Align ground-truth QA evidence regions to detected (or annotated) layout nodes via IoU overlap ≥ 0.5; when IoU < 0.5, assign the evidence span to the nearest detected region by centroid distance. (3) Build the per-page typed evidence graph with rule-based edges (Caption-of, Adjacent, Up/Down/Left/Right). (4) For each QA pair, extract the shortest path in the evidence graph traversing all aligned evidence regions — this forms the traversal template. (5) Verbalize the traversal template into a structured chain-of-thought: 'Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]' covering 2-4 hop lengths. The InfographicVQA training split (~24K QA pairs) is the primary training source — it is per-page, layout-intensive, and in-distribution with respect to the primary evaluation target. PMC-OA scientific pages supplement this corpus with figure+caption+table triplets characteristic of academic document layouts.

DocHop-QA is audited on Day 1 for within-page-amenable instances (all evidence BBox regions on a single page). If this audit yields ≥500 instances, they are included as a supplementary training source. If fewer than 500 instances qualify (expected given cross-document dominance), DocHop-QA is dropped from training and this decision is documented in the paper.

For the EMNLP 2026 submission, cross-page PageRef linking is scoped out — per-page graphs are used throughout; rule-based cross-reference linking is explicitly presented as future work for the AAAI 2027 extended version.

Evaluation plan:
(1) Day 1 prerequisite: Zero-shot Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on InfographicVQA and WikiMixQA oracle setting to establish actual baselines. This is a precondition for interpretable contribution framing — the paper cannot use previously reported figures from different backbones as anchors, and the WikiMixQA oracle estimate (~20–30% for a non-fine-tuned 8B model, consistent with the 23–27% range for larger open-source models) must be confirmed.
(2) Primary benchmark — primary contribution claim: InfographicVQA (per-page, layout-intensive, active leaderboard). Report: (a) overall ANLS, base Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct vs. LHEC-fine-tuned; (b) hard multi-hop layout subset ANLS (questions requiring ≥2 evidence source types per Day 0 annotation audit), where the largest gains are expected and the primary contribution claim is grounded.
(3) Exploratory secondary benchmark: WikiMixQA oracle setting (table+chart provided directly, multi-hop synthesis; open-source models score 14–27% vs. proprietary ~70%, near-random for 4-choice MCQ with 25% random baseline). At WikiMixQA oracle evaluation, LHEC (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct fine-tuned) receives the HTML table and chart image as direct multimodal inputs without DocLayout-YOLO preprocessing; the model applies its trained cross-modal traversal reasoning to these two provided modalities. We hypothesize that QLoRA fine-tuning on typed layout traversal chains conditions the model to reason sequentially across modality boundaries — a capacity that transfers when table and chart are provided as separate inputs without explicit node IDs, since the underlying cross-modal synthesis step (reading a table value, then locating and interpreting the corresponding chart element) is structurally identical whether framed via graph node IDs or as direct multimodal inputs. The Wikidoc/retrieval setting is excluded because LHEC's per-page graphs cannot resolve evidence spread across multiple rendered pages. Given the near-random, scale-invariant open-source failure pattern on WikiMixQA oracle, gains from traversal fine-tuning are uncertain. If gains are ≤5% over the Day 1 baseline, the WikiMixQA result is reported as a documented negative — establishing the boundary of layout traversal training's transferability to cross-modal table+chart synthesis — and the contribution is framed entirely through the InfographicVQA hard multi-hop subset. This contingency is treated as the expected primary scenario, not a fallback.
(4) Scope-acknowledged secondary benchmark: DocHop-QA within-page-only subset (after audit). Report LHEC vs. base model on this subset with explicit framing: 'LHEC addresses within-page layout traversal; results are reported on the ~X% of DocHop-QA instances where all evidence is contained within a single page.'
(5) Regression checks: DocVQA (~96% for base, near ceiling — regression check only), ChartQA (near ceiling — regression check only).
(6) Zero-shot general regression suite: TextVQA, GQA, POPE, MMBench, SEED-Bench, RealWorldQA — base Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct vs. fine-tuned LHEC, confirming no general regression from document-specific QLoRA fine-tuning.

Baselines: vanilla Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (zero-shot), ARGUS (single-element grounding), PDF-VQA LoSpa (extractive element-selection, re-implemented on DocHop-QA within-page subset and InfographicVQA), MGA-VQA (direct comparison using public codebase on InfographicVQA and WikiMixQA oracle).",

DocCogito is a unified framework that integrates global layout perception with structured, region-grounded reasoning.

The paper reports InfoVQA results as accuracy metrics, not ANLS scores:

The framework employs **Qwen3-VL** as its foundation:
- Qwen3-VL-Instruct-4B
- Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B

The five primitives are:

- **Read**: "Extract textual content from the selected region"
- **Filter**: "Filter candidates using predicates (e.g., key contains 'Revenue')"
- **Compare**: "Apply comparison metrics (eq, max, min) to identify values"
- **Aggregate**: "Combine multiple values via summation or concatenation"

The paper does **not** explicitly model typed edges between layout regions. Instead, it uses a global layout prior token and region-grounded confidence signals. The region reward (Equation 13) encourages "high confidence to correct layout regions" but lacks explicit relational graphs.

- **VSC cold-start**: 4,000 curated samples from DocVQA categories

I now have all I need. DocCogito (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct backbone, 78.6% InfoVQA, no explicit typed inter-region edges, 4-stage GRPO pipeline) is confirmed concurrent work. Critically: its 78.6% with complex training is below the Qwen2.5-VL-72B zero-shot baseline (84.2%), which actually *strengthens* LHEC's position — implicit layout tokens + operation sequences are insufficient for hard multi-hop questions. The revision is a targeted minor fix.

{
  "title": "Layout-Structured Multi-Hop Evidence Chains for Complex Document Reasoning",
  "project_name": "layout_hop_evidence_chain",
  "source": "web_research",
  "change_type": "minor",
  "core_problem": "Complex document questions require synthesizing evidence from multiple layout regions within a single page — reading a value from a table, referencing the adjacent caption, then cross-checking with an embedded chart — but no existing method trains a generative VLM to produce explicit multi-hop traversal traces across Table, Figure, Caption, and TextBlock nodes while preserving typed spatial relationships between semantic layout elements. Models either flatten the document into a token sequence (losing inter-region structure) or navigate page-by-page (missing within-page region-to-region links), or use implicit graph propagation with no supervisable chain-of-thought.

The empirical gap is well-established for WITHIN-PAGE multi-hop layout reasoning: WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) demonstrates that within-page multi-hop table-and-chart reasoning is severely challenging for current models — in the oracle/direct-context setting (table and chart provided directly), proprietary models achieve ~70% (GPT-4o: 71.42%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 70.82%, Gemini-2.0-Pro: 69.53%) while open-source VLMs score only 14–27% (InternVL2.5-78B: 27.37%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 23.17%, Llama-3.2-11B: 14.08%); in the Wikidoc/retrieval setting, GPT-4o is the only model exceeding 50% (55.24%). Notably, the oracle-setting open-source performance (23–27%) is near-random for a 4-choice MCQ (25% baseline) and barely scales from 1B to 78B parameters — indicating a fundamental cross-modal synthesis limitation rather than purely a layout traversal gap. This large open-source gap in the oracle setting directly quantifies the within-region synthesis difficulty that LHEC targets, while the scale-invariance pattern motivates making the InfographicVQA hard subset the primary contribution claim. InfographicVQA's hard multi-hop layout questions (requiring ≥2 layout-region hops across charts, tables, captions, and text blocks in a single infographic) represent the primary per-page evaluation front where base VLMs that treat pages as flat images fail to exploit spatial relationships.

Two prior works come closest. PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) already builds typed Logical Relation graphs (parent-child hierarchical) and Spatial Relation graphs (8-directional: top/bottom/left/right and four diagonals) over document nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — graph construction over these node types is therefore not novel. But PDF-VQA's LoSpa model is fully extractive (predicts an element index via GCN, then retrieves OCR text from that region), produces no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought, and is evaluated only on the proprietary PDF-VQA PubMed dataset. MGA-VQA (arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025) builds a spatial graph from OCR-detected text bounding boxes with untyped proximity/similarity edges and propagates through a 3-layer implicit GCN; its text-box nodes miss figure and chart regions entirely, its edges carry no semantic type labels, and all outputs are extractive spans with no traversal chain-of-thought.

The structured gap is: no method trains a generative VLM to verbalize step-by-step multi-hop traversal across typed layout-region nodes within a page — the exact capability required to answer questions that chain a table value through an Adjacent edge to its Caption and then through a Caption-of edge into a referenced Figure.",
  "opportunity": "InfographicVQA (WACV 2022, leaderboard active) is the **primary** evaluation target and the primary contribution claim: it is genuinely per-page and layout-intensive, requiring joint reasoning over charts, tables, maps, and text blocks within single infographic images. The current SOTA is 88.4% ANLS achieved by Small Drafts, Big Verdict (arXiv:2510.20812, Oct 2025), a training-free speculative decoding ensemble that combines five small draft VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, MiMo-VL-7B-RL, InternVL3-8B, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, Ovis2.5-9B) with GPT-4o as the verdict model — this result requires proprietary inference at test time and a multi-model ensemble. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B as the verdict model instead of GPT-4o, the method achieves 86.7%. The best open-source single-model zero-shot result is Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct at 84.2% ANLS (as reported in the SV paper). The most directly comparable concurrent trained 8B model is DocCogito (arXiv:2603.07494, March 2026), which achieves 78.6% ANLS on InfographicVQA using the same Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct backbone with a complex four-stage training pipeline (layout pretraining + VSC cold start + rejection sampling + GRPO). The fact that DocCogito's elaborate implicit-layout-token training achieves 78.6% — notably below both the Qwen2.5-VL-72B zero-shot result (84.2%) and the expected Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct zero-shot range (80–84%) — confirms that implicit layout representation learning with operation-sequence supervision is insufficient for the hardest multi-hop layout questions, directly motivating LHEC's explicit typed graph traversal approach. No method exceeds 90% (human performance is ~98%), confirming this benchmark is not at ceiling. LHEC targets a complementary and different efficiency point in the design space: a single trained open-source 8B model with intrinsic multi-hop layout reasoning capability, requiring no ensemble and no proprietary model at inference time.

The actual fine-tuning backbone is Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, whose InfoVQA baseline must be established via zero-shot evaluation on Day 1 of the project (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct score is unconfirmed in any public source as of May 2026 — likely in the 80–84 range based on scaling trends from Qwen2.5-VL-7B). Regardless of the overall ANLS level, hard multi-hop layout questions — those requiring the model to traverse ≥2 typed layout regions to compose the answer, identified via InfographicVQA's evidence-source category annotations — are the defensible hard subset where LHEC's explicit traversal training targets a meaningful gap over the base model. The Day 0 hard-subset audit (described in the approach) will determine whether the hard subset count supports statistical significance (≥200) or preliminary (100–200) framing.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) is an **exploratory secondary** evaluation target: it benchmarks multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia. In the oracle/direct-context setting (table and chart provided directly), proprietary models achieve ~70% (GPT-4o: 71.42%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 70.82%, Gemini-2.0-Pro: 69.53%), while open-source VLMs score only 14–27% even with direct evidence access (InternVL2.5-78B: 27.37%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 23.17%). Critically, this oracle-setting open-source performance is near-random for a 4-choice MCQ (25% random baseline) and barely scales from 1B to 78B parameters — indicating that the failure reflects a fundamental cross-modal table+chart synthesis limitation rather than a layout traversal gap that typed graph training alone can bridge. LHEC evaluates WikiMixQA exclusively in the oracle setting; at evaluation, LHEC (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct fine-tuned) receives the HTML table and chart image as direct multimodal inputs without DocLayout-YOLO preprocessing — the trained cross-modal traversal reasoning is applied directly to these two provided modalities. The Wikidoc/retrieval setting is excluded because LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address evidence spread across multiple rendered pages (Wikipedia articles average 24.18 rendered pages). The Day 1 zero-shot Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline on WikiMixQA oracle will establish whether traversal fine-tuning yields non-trivial gains (>5%). If gains are ≤5% over the Day 1 baseline, the WikiMixQA result is reported as a documented negative — establishing the limits of layout traversal training for cross-modal table+chart synthesis — and the contribution is framed entirely through the InfographicVQA hard multi-hop subset. This contingency plan is the expected primary contribution scenario given the near-random, scale-invariant failure pattern.

DocHop-QA (arXiv:2508.15851, NeurIPS 2025 track) is explicitly a cross-DOCUMENT benchmark (its own paper reports multi-document reasoning dominates overall). LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address cross-document failure modes. DocHop-QA is therefore used ONLY as a supplementary training corpus after a Day 1 audit: instances where all BBox-annotated evidence regions fall within a single page are extracted and used for within-page traversal chain synthesis; the cross-document majority of the 11,379 instances is excluded. If the within-page audit yields fewer than 500 usable instances, DocHop-QA is dropped from training entirely and the claim of using it is removed.

BRIDGE (March 2026, arXiv:2603.07931) provides grounded multi-hop evidence annotations for long scientific documents and confirms no proposed method resolves the within-page cross-region gap it diagnoses; it is a strong secondary evaluation target for the AAAI 2027 extended version. The combination of DocLayout-YOLO layout detection (with GT annotation fallback for infographics, detailed in approach) + rule-based typed graph + generative VLM fine-tuned on explicit verbalized traversal chains is architecturally distinct from PDF-VQA (extractive element-index model), MGA-VQA (implicit GCN on OCR boxes), LayoutLLM/DocLayLLM (text layout embeddings with coordinate-anchored CoT steps, no spatial graph), DocCogito (implicit learned layout prior tokens + VSC operation sequences, no typed inter-region edges, 4-stage GRPO training), and Small Drafts, Big Verdict (inference-time ensemble requiring GPT-4o), buildable entirely from open components, and executable within 15 days targeting EMNLP 2026 ARR (May 25, 2026).",
  "landscape": "Multi-page document VQA methods include GRAM (learnable document tokens), Hi-VT5 (hierarchical page summaries), Doc-V* (April 2026, arXiv:2604.13731, coarse-to-fine agentic page navigation), AVIR (Jan 2026, adaptive visual retrieval for SlideVQA). Within-page multi-hop reasoning: ARGUS (CVPR 2025) grounds single visual elements with bounding boxes in CoT chains; GCoT (March 2025) generates coordinate-grounded reasoning steps; MAGIC-VQA (ACL 2025 Findings) uses commonsense knowledge graphs for inference.

LayoutLLM (arXiv:2404.05225, CVPR 2024) introduces LayoutCoT, a three-step layout chain-of-thought module (Question Analysis → Relevant Area Concentration → Answer Formation) that generates text reasoning steps augmented with bounding-box coordinate anchors over document layout text, achieving +3.45% on DocVQA zero-shot (74.27% ANLS). LayoutLLM uses a LayoutLMv3-based document encoder with 2D positional text embeddings — there is no spatial graph, no typed inter-region edges, and no visual region detector; the 'Relevant Area Concentration' step outputs the union bounding box of relevant text spans rather than traversing detected layout regions. LayoutCoT does not evaluate on InfographicVQA or WikiMixQA. LHEC extends this direction on three axes: (a) LHEC uses DocLayout-YOLO to ground reasoning in visually detected spatial regions (Table, Figure, Caption, TextBlock) rather than text layout embeddings; (b) LHEC assigns typed spatial edges between detected nodes (Caption-of, Adjacent, Up/Down/Left/Right) enabling graph-structured multi-hop traversal across heterogeneous region types including figure and chart nodes invisible to text-only encoders; (c) LHEC trains on explicit node-ID traversal traces (Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]) that are directly supervisable as structured chain-of-thought, rather than question-type reasoning steps. DocLayLLM (arXiv:2408.15045, CVPR 2025), a follow-on from the same lineage, integrates visual patches (196 tokens), 2D positional tokens, and text into an LLM backbone via lightweight projectors with CoT Pre-training on layout-type, table-structure, and geometry tasks plus CoT Annealing; it achieves 76.59% on InfographicVQA ANLS. DocLayLLM similarly uses no spatial graph and no typed inter-region edges — its table-structure CoT operates within detected table boundaries, not across heterogeneous layout region types.

DocCogito (arXiv:2603.07494, March 2026) is direct concurrent work and must be cited and differentiated from. DocCogito uses Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct as its backbone — the identical model LHEC fine-tunes — and introduces a lightweight layout tower that distills page structure into learnable global layout prior tokens injected into the LLM backbone. It trains the model via a four-stage progressive pipeline (layout perception pretraining on 20K DocVQA samples → VSC-guided cold start on 4K curated samples → rejection sampling → GRPO with augmented region-confidence rewards) to generate Visual-Semantic Chain (VSC) traces: deterministic sequences of five atomic operations (Select: choose a semantic region using structural or key cues; Read: extract textual content from the selected region; Filter: filter candidates using predicates; Compare: apply comparison metrics to identify values; Aggregate: combine multiple values via summation or concatenation) over document regions. DocCogito-8B achieves 78.6% ANLS on InfographicVQA and state-of-the-art on 4 of 6 evaluated benchmarks (DocVQA, ChartQA, WTQ, OCRBench). An ablation reported in the paper shows that removing the layout tower decreases InfoVQA performance by 1.6 points, indicating the tower contributes modestly over the multi-stage trained backbone alone. Critically, DocCogito does not model explicit typed inter-region edges — the layout tower produces global prior tokens without Caption-of, Adjacent, or directional relational structure, and the VSC operations do not reference node-to-node edge traversal paths. The notable finding that DocCogito-8B achieves only 78.6% despite complex four-stage GRPO training — below the Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct zero-shot result of 84.2% and below the expected Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct zero-shot range of 80–84% — confirms that implicit layout token learning with operation-sequence supervision is insufficient to bridge the hard multi-hop layout question gap, motivating LHEC's alternative of explicit typed spatial graphs with verifiable node-ID traversal traces. LHEC is architecturally differentiated from DocCogito on four axes: (a) LHEC builds an explicit rule-based typed spatial graph (Caption-of by 150px vertical proximity; Adjacent by shared column/row boundary; Up/Down/Left/Right from center-point geometry following GraphDoc taxonomy) rather than learning implicit layout prior tokens via a separate trained tower; (b) LHEC trains on node-ID traversal traces (Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]) that are directly verifiable against the constructed graph — ground-truth validity of each hop can be independently checked — whereas DocCogito's VSC operation sequences have no ground-truth graph against which Select/Read/Filter steps can be independently verified; (c) LHEC requires only QLoRA fine-tuning with no layout pretraining stage, no GRPO, and no rejection sampling, making the training pipeline substantially simpler and the compute budget smaller; (d) LHEC's explicit edge types (Caption-of, Adjacent, directional) directly encode the spatial semantics most relevant to multi-hop layout questions — navigating from a data cell to its caption to the referenced chart — which are absent from DocCogito's global layout tokens. DocCogito must be included as a comparison baseline on InfographicVQA.

PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) is an important predecessor that must be cited and differentiated from. It builds both a typed Logical Relation graph (LR graph: binary parent-child hierarchical edges) and a typed Spatial Relation graph (SR graph: 8-directional edges — top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) over document element nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — the same node types LHEC uses. Its LoSpa model propagates via GCN to predict the index of the document element containing the answer (fully extractive: answer is OCR text retrieved from that region). PDF-VQA is evaluated only on its own proprietary PubMed Central dataset and contains no verbalized chain-of-thought. LHEC's novel contribution relative to PDF-VQA is the training of a generative VLM to verbalize traversal traces step-by-step ('Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]') as a directly supervisable chain-of-thought.

MGA-VQA (Nov 2025, arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025 track) is the second closest prior work and the most important direct comparison target: it uses OCR-detected text boxes as nodes (no figure/chart nodes), untyped proximity and semantic-similarity edges with scalar weights, a 3-layer GCN for implicit propagation, and extractive span outputs; it evaluates on FUNSD, CORD, SROIE, DocVQA, STE-VQA, RICO — DocVQA is included but all outputs are extractive spans from OCR boxes; no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought is produced and figure/chart regions are invisible to the model. LHEC differentiates on four axes: semantic layout region nodes, typed edges, verbalized traversal traces, and generative output. Public code at github.com/ahmad-shirazi/MGAVQA enables direct comparison.
